sentences.text: Caryonosuchus was a reptile that lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
Its snout features unique horn-like bumps on the upper jaw bones and displays rough ornamentation consisting of grooves and bony ridges.
The only known fossil of this animal is a nearly complete front part of the skull and lower jaw.
The unique horn-like bumps and rough ornamentation on its snout distinguish it from other known reptiles.
The specimen was collected from the Adamantina Formation within the Bauru Basin, near the city of Presidente Prudente in southwest São Paulo State.

Before its formal description, the fossil was tentatively assigned to the genus Sphagesaurus, but researchers determined it represented a new genus and species, which was named in 2011 by Kellner, Campos, Riff, and de Andrade.
The species name honors Llewellyn Ivor Price, who originally described the holotype — the specimen the species is based on — in an unpublished manuscript.
Phylogenetic analysis classifies Caryonosuchus as an advanced member of the sphagesaurid family, specifically within the subfamily Sphagesaurinae.
Caryonosuchus lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago in southeastern Brazil.
